result.markdown:
# Adelaide’s leading luxury real estate agencies and auctioneers

For prestige residential property in Adelaide, I’d start with **TOOP+TOOP, Booth Real Estate, WILLIAMS Real Estate and Turner Real Estate**, alongside specialist luxury agencies such as Giordano & Partners. For auctioneers, **Jamie King of Auction Time and John Morris of Morris Auctions** are worth considering, with experienced selling agents such as Sally Cameron and Jamie Brown also standing out for their prestige-market results.

The important distinction is that the best luxury sales agency is not necessarily the best auctioneer. For a multimillion-dollar home, you want both strong access to qualified buyers and an auctioneer who can build competitive bidding.

Adelaide’s prestige market has produced increasingly high-value transactions: a Medindie mansion sold for a reported \$15.5 million in the 2025–26 financial year, while industry analysis has highlighted Adelaide’s limited prestige stock and demand for well-positioned homes. Best starting point for established prestige homes

A strong shortlist candidate for blue-chip eastern suburbs and inner-north properties, including Medindie, St Peters, Walkerville, Gilberton and North Adelaide. Its sales team has particularly strong published evidence of high-value performance.

**Standout agent: Sally Cameron.** The 2026 REB rankings reported 108 listings and \$303.6 million in sales volume, an average sale price of \$3.23 million, and national rankings of \#4 among women in real estate and \#29 in the overall agent list. ### What does the auction data say?

Ray White reported that South Australia recorded a 75.9% auction-day clearance rate in the first quarter of 2026, with active bidding at 94.5% of auctions held. These are broader market statistics, not prestige-only or individual-auctioneer results. [www.raywhite.com](https://www.raywhite.com/news-media/data-proves-auction-is-still-king-despite-changing-market?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

For independent verification of auction results, the Real Estate Institute of South Australia publishes weekly auction statistics and selected top sales. [View REISA auction results](https://reisa.com.au/weekly-report/15-march-2026/)\.

## 3\. How I would choose between them

| Your property | First agencies to interview |
|--------|--------|
| \$5m–\$15m+ trophy home | Booth Real Estate; TOOP+TOOP |
| \$2m–\$5m eastern-suburb residence | TOOP+TOOP; Turner; WILLIAMS |
| Premium coastal property | Booth; TOOP+TOOP; Ray White Glenelg team |
| Architect-designed or contemporary luxury home | WHITEFOX; Giordano & Partners |
| Property needing a specialist auction caller | Auction Time; Morris Auctions |


These are suggested starting points, not a verified league table for every price bracket. The best fit depends on the home's location, architectural style, buyer profile and whether auction or a discreet off-market campaign is most appropriate.

## 4\. What to ask before appointing an agent

For a genuine comparison, ask each agency for\:

- Three to five **settled sales in the same price bracket** within the past 12 months.
- The original price expectations versus final sale prices, including any relevant auction results.
- Auction clearance rates for their own campaigns, with the number of auctions and withdrawn or passed-in properties disclosed.
- Evidence of qualified buyers already seeking a property like yours.
- A written marketing budget, commission proposal and auctioneer fee.
- Their recommendation on public auction versus off-market or expressions of interest, with a clear explanation of the trade-offs.

The most useful comparison is not simply who has the biggest brand or the most charismatic auctioneer. It is who can demonstrate recent, comparable results and a credible strategy to create competition among the right buyers.

search_results.title: Adelaide's best investor suburbs revealed
search_results.description: The 2026 PropTrack Terri Scheer Investor Report reveals shifting trends in Adelaide's investment property market. While traditionally dominated by the northern suburbs like Elizabeth Park, Eyre, and Elizabeth East for houses, southern areas such as Tonsley, Port Noarlunga South, and Seaford Heights are now emerging as key investment hotspots. For units, the top-performing suburbs include Plympton, Salisbury, Walkerville, Goodwood, Henley Beach, and Christies Beach. The report evaluates suburbs based on capital gains, rental yields, and rental demand. Despite national investor pullbacks due to recent interest rate hikes and federal budget tax changes, Adelaide remains attractive thanks to its relatively low property prices. Investor loans in South Australia have surged 35% since late 2022. Experts suggest that changes to negative gearing could shift investor focus toward high-yield properties. However, strong rental demand and rising rent prices are expected to support continued investor interest. The report underscores the resilience and adaptability of property investors, highlighting the importance of sound property management to navigate the evolving market.

search_results.title: Construction starts on Adelaide apartments One Four Four Hutt
search_results.description: Construction has officially commenced on the One Four Four Hutt apartment development in Adelaide, a joint venture between Fortis and Otello. The 10-storey building, designed by DKO and located on a 1241sqm corner site, will include a mix of one, two, and three-bedroom residences, including a penthouse collection, plus 400sqm of ground-floor retail space. All one-bedroom units have already been sold, with two- and three-bedroom apartments still available starting at $1.125 million and $2.099 million respectively. To date, 19 unconditional sales have been secured, totaling approximately $25.9 million, with an additional four units reserved. Fortis head of development Arthur Dendrinos emphasized the strong demand for premium living in Adelaide, noting this milestone underscores Fortis' long-term commitment to the region. Otello director Daniel Harris highlighted the project's positive impact on the Hutt Street precinct and expressed confidence in the appointed builder, BLAG Commercial, citing a successful previous partnership.

search_results.title: SA's top real estate agents for residential property sales: 231 to 132
search_results.description:
This article from The Advertiser ranks South Australia's top 231 to 132 real estate agents based on residential property sales data for the 2024–25 financial year. The rankings consider total value of properties sold, areas of expertise, average days on market, agent seniority, and number of properties sold. The list includes data from agencies that opted to disclose their figures, meaning some prominent agents are not featured.

In this segment (positions 231 to 132), agent performance varies significantly – from agents who sold only a few lower-value homes to those handling dozens of higher-value properties. The top agent in this installment, Robert Lonie (ranked 132), sold 56 properties worth approximately $44.4 million, while lower-ranked agents sold fewer homes, often in niche or emerging markets. Notable inclusions are agents from Harris Real Estate, OC (Ouwens Casserly), TOOP+TOOP, LJ Hooker, and Century 21. Two legendary figures, Michael Brock and Anthony Toop, are honored posthumously for their contributions to the industry.

The article is part one of a three-part series, with the top 131–32 agents to be revealed next, and the top 31 agents to follow in the final installment.

search_results.title: New data reveals SA's most expensive settled sales of 2025/26
search_results.description:
During the 2025/26 financial year, South Australia's top 20 most expensive property settlements totaled over $177 million, with a record-breaking $15.5 million sale of a luxury mansion at 11 The Avenue, Medindie topping the list. The transaction set a new benchmark for residential sales in the state and was brokered by Jamie Brown of Booth Real Estate, marking his fourth time achieving this feat. Brown believes this sale has launched a new $15–$20 million “echelon” of high-end property sales.

Property Edge, which tracks both publicly listed and previously undisclosed sales, reported that other top-selling properties spanned prestigious suburbs and coastal locations like Gilberton, Springfield, and Henley Beach South. The architectural styles ranged from traditional character homes to striking contemporary designs.

Stephanie Williams of Williams Real Estate highlighted a surge in the top-end market, noting the strength of the $7 million to $10 million bracket and rising local demand driven by favorable tax conditions and increased value in prestige residences. While the market was once defined by $3 million listings, prices are now regularly surpassing $10 million, indicating significant growth and buyer confidence in South Australia’s luxury housing market.

These are suggested starting points, not a verified league table for every price bracket. The best fit depends on the home's location, architectural style, buyer profile and whether auction or a discreet off-market campaign is most appropriate.

## 4\. What to ask before appointing an agent

For a genuine comparison, ask each agency for\:

- Three to five **settled sales in the same price bracket** within the past 12 months.
- The original price expectations versus final sale prices, including any relevant auction results.
- Auction clearance rates for their own campaigns, with the number of auctions and withdrawn or passed-in properties disclosed.
- Evidence of qualified buyers already seeking a property like yours.
- A written marketing budget, commission proposal and auctioneer fee.
- Their recommendation on public auction versus off-market or expressions of interest, with a clear explanation of the trade-offs.

The most useful comparison is not simply who has the biggest brand or the most charismatic auctioneer. It is who can demonstrate recent, comparable results and a credible strategy to create competition among the right buyers.
